name: Milion.Ai Connector
author: milionai

sections.description:
Milion.Ai helps businesses get found on Google and named in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews). This plugin connects your WordPress site to your Milion.Ai account, so the work you approve there is applied here safely.

  • Publishing: articles you approve in Milion.Ai are published with title, excerpt, categories, tags, featured image, meta description, focus keyword (Yoast SEO or Rank Math) and structured data (Article and FAQ schema).
  • Site fixes with undo: fixes you approve (SEO titles, meta descriptions, image alt text, insecure http:// links) are applied to existing posts and pages. The previous values are kept so every fix can be undone, content changes also create a normal WordPress revision, and a page someone edited after it was checked is never overwritten.
  • Comments inbox (optional): approved comments can be sent to your Milion.Ai inbox, where replies are drafted, approved by you, and posted back under your chosen author.
  • Site profile for AI assistants: serves an /llms.txt summary of your business and key pages, and adds your organization’s structured data (name, logo, contact details, social profiles) to the home page. Both are written in Milion.Ai, where you review them before publishing.
  • IndexNow (optional): notify Bing, Yandex, Naver, Seznam and other participating search engines whenever any post is published or updated. The key file is served for you.
  • Redirections and 404 monitor (optional): redirect old addresses, mark removed pages, and see which missing addresses are being asked for.
  • Sitemaps (optional): XML sitemaps with images, plus news and video sitemaps.
  • Image SEO (optional): images without alt text get one automatically when the page is shown.

Every request between your site and Milion.Ai is signed with a secret only the two share, expires after five minutes and can’t be replayed. The plugin has no tracking and adds no front-end scripts.

A Milion.Ai account is required. Every account starts with a free 14-day trial; paid plans are listed at milion.ai. The plugin itself is free and GPL-licensed.

External services

This plugin connects to the following services. Nothing is sent before you connect the plugin or turn the feature on.

Milion.Ai (https://app.milion.ai), the service this plugin connects to.
* When an administrator presses “Run the free check” (shown before the site is connected): the administrator’s browser opens Milion.Ai’s free AI visibility check with this site’s name and address filled in. Nothing else is sent, and nothing is sent before the button is pressed.
* When an administrator presses “Connect to Milion.Ai”: the administrator’s browser is sent to Milion.Ai with this site’s address, its name, the address to return to and a random one-time value. On return, the plugin sends the one-time token it received and that value to Milion.Ai and receives the site’s connection code. Nothing is sent before the button is pressed.
* When you connect: Milion.Ai sends signed requests to your site to publish approved articles, read a post’s title, address, excerpt, search and sharing settings, categories, tags and content before proposing a change, apply or undo approved fixes, and post approved comment replies.
* When someone opens the Search tab (at most once an hour) or presses “Check again” there: the plugin sends its connection ID and a signature to Milion.Ai and receives the site’s Google Search results (clicks, impressions, top pages and searches) that Milion.Ai holds from Search Console. Nothing about your site’s content or visitors is sent.
* When an administrator opens the Milion.Ai screen in WordPress (at most once every ten minutes) or presses “Check again”: the plugin sends its connection ID and a signature to Milion.Ai and receives the account’s status (active, on trial, payment failed, paused), plan, monthly allowance and the number of fixes, articles and comments waiting. Nothing about your site’s content or visitors is sent.
* When “Comments” is on: each approved comment’s ID, the post title and address, the commenter’s name, the comment text and its date are sent to Milion.Ai. Email and IP addresses are never sent.
* When “AI crawler visits” is on: once an hour, the number of visits per day, per AI crawler (identified by its user agent, e.g. GPTBot or ClaudeBot) and per page path is sent to Milion.Ai. Requests from people are not recorded.
* Redirect rules, the list of missing addresses and the on/off state of the plugin’s features are stored on your site. Milion.Ai reads and changes them only when someone on your account opens or uses SEO → WordPress site.
* Terms: https://milion.ai/terms/ · Privacy policy: https://milion.ai/privacy/

IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org), when “IndexNow” is on.
* When a public post is published or updated, its address, your site’s host name and your IndexNow key are sent so participating search engines can recrawl it.
* About IndexNow: https://www.indexnow.org/ · The endpoint is operated with Microsoft Bing: https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement

Featured images: when Milion.Ai publishes an article with a featured image, WordPress downloads that image into your media library from the address Milion.Ai provides: a Pexels stock photo (images.pexels.com; https://www.pexels.com/terms-of-service/, https://www.pexels.com/privacy-policy/) or a cover image generated by Milion.Ai (app.milion.ai). The same happens when you approve a new featured image for an existing post in Milion.Ai.

Privacy

The plugin stores its connection settings in your WordPress options. It does not track visitors, set cookies or load external scripts. With “AI crawler visits” on, it counts requests whose user agent belongs to an AI crawler; requests from people are ignored. If you turn on comment syncing, mention in your privacy policy that comments may be processed by Milion.Ai to help you reply.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (Plugins → Add New → search “Milion.Ai Connector”).
  2. In Milion.Ai, open Connections → WordPress plugin, enter your site address and copy the connection code.
  3. In WordPress, open Milion.Ai → Settings, paste the code, choose the author to publish as, and save. Turn on the optional features you want under Milion.Ai → Features.
  4. Back in Milion.Ai, click Verify.
sections.faq:
Does Milion.Ai publish anything without my approval?

Only if you turn on auto-publish for this site in Milion.Ai, and only for content that passes every policy check. Everything else waits in your Approvals queue. Site fixes are always approved one by one (or “apply all” for a type) by a person.

Which SEO plugins are supported?

Yoast SEO and Rank Math: titles, meta descriptions and focus keywords are written to their fields. Without an SEO plugin, the plugin outputs the meta description and title itself.

Can I undo a fix?

Yes. Every applied fix can be undone from Milion.Ai. If the page was edited after the fix, its content is left alone (use WordPress revisions instead) so your later edits are never lost.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating stops all communication. Deleting removes the plugin’s settings and its undo backups. Posts, comments, SEO titles, descriptions and schema it created stay, because they are part of your content.
sections.changelog:
0.9.0

  • Search tab: your site’s Google clicks, impressions, click rate and position for the last 28 days against the 28 before, a daily line, and the pages and searches that bring the most clicks, with each page’s score beside it. From the Search Console data Milion.Ai holds for your account.
  • Local SEO (optional): your business name, address, phone, opening hours and map position as LocalBusiness structured data on the home page, and as a block anywhere with the [milion_business] shortcode.
  • Product SEO for WooCommerce (optional): adds the brand, GTIN and return policy to product structured data (WooCommerce’s own, or Rank Math’s when it is active), lists products missing a picture, description, price, identifier or brand, and keeps cart, checkout and account pages out of the sitemap.
  • Role manager: under Settings, choose which roles besides administrators may open each tab. Only roles that can edit content can be given one; Settings stays with administrators.
  • The sitemap now includes content types registered by other plugins, such as products.

0.8.0

  • Redirections (optional): send old or mistyped addresses to the right page (301, 302 or 307), or mark a page as removed (410). End an old address with * to cover everything under it. Manage them in WordPress under Milion.Ai → Redirects, or from Milion.Ai.
  • 404 monitor (optional): lists the missing addresses people and search engines ask for, with how often, and a “Redirect it” button. Only the address is kept: no IP address, browser or referrer.
  • Sitemap (optional): an XML sitemap of every published post, page and public content type with its images, listed in robots.txt, leaving out pages kept out of search results. Optional news sitemap (posts from the last two days) and video sitemap (pages with a YouTube or Vimeo video).
  • Image SEO (optional): images without alt text get one as the page is shown, made from the image’s name. Nothing is saved to the database and existing alt text is never replaced.
  • Features is now a status page: what your site is doing now (redirects, broken addresses, published pages, average page score), one suggested feature to turn on next, and a switch for everything else.
  • Before connecting, the Account tab offers Milion.Ai’s free check: does an AI assistant recommend your business?
  • One-click connect: press Connect to Milion.Ai, confirm on Milion.Ai and come back connected. Pasting a connection code still works.
  • New look on every tab in Milion.Ai’s own colours, with icons, score rings, a score breakdown on Page scores and request bars on broken addresses.
  • New Agent tab: shows whether the Milion.Ai agent works on this site, how far it may go (ask first, or do the safe things automatically), what its last run did and what is waiting for you. The agent’s settings are in Milion.Ai.
  • All of these are off until you turn them on, and each can be switched from Milion.Ai under SEO → WordPress site.

0.7.0

  • Account: see in WordPress whether your Milion.Ai account is active, its plan and renewal or trial date, how much of this month’s allowance is used, and what is waiting for your approval, with a “Check again” button.
  • A Milion.Ai menu in the WordPress sidebar with five tabs: Account, Features (what the plugin does, with switches for IndexNow, comment replies and AI crawler visits), Page scores, Settings and Help. The settings screen moved here from Settings → Milion.Ai.
  • Page score: a score out of 100 and a checklist for every post and page (focus keyword, search result, content, sharing and images), in a box on the post editor and in a list under Page scores. It is worked out on your site and sends nothing anywhere.
  • Page settings: from Milion.Ai you can now change an existing post or page’s headline, address and excerpt, its canonical address, whether search engines may index it, its focus keyword, the title, description and image used when it is shared, its featured image, and its categories and tags. Each change is applied only after you approve it, and can be undone.
  • Changing a page’s address redirects the old address to the new one.
  • Search and sharing settings are saved in Yoast SEO or Rank Math when one is active; without an SEO plugin this plugin prints them itself.

0.6.0

  • Page structured data: Milion.Ai can add JSON-LD (FAQ, service, breadcrumbs) to existing pages and posts once you approve it, with undo. It is printed in the page head like the schema of articles published from Milion.Ai.

0.5.0

  • AI crawler visits (opt-in): see in Milion.Ai which AI crawlers and assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Meta, Amazon, Apple and others) read which pages of your site.

0.4.0

  • Site profile for search engines and AI assistants: serves /llms.txt and adds your organization’s structured data (JSON-LD) to the home page, both written in Milion.Ai and published from there. Deleting the plugin removes them.

0.3.0

  • IndexNow and comment syncing are now opt-in (off until you turn them on in Settings → Milion.Ai).
  • Clearer descriptions of what each option sends, and a full list of external services in this readme.
  • Deleting the plugin also removes its undo backups.

0.2.0

  • Site fixes with undo: SEO title, meta description, image alt text and https links on existing pages.
  • Meta description output (without an SEO plugin) now covers pages as well as posts.

0.1.0

  • First release.

screenshots.caption: Features: what your site is doing now, the one feature worth turning on next, and a switch for everything else.
Agent: what the Milion.Ai agent did on this site in its last run, and what is waiting for you.
Page scores: a score out of 100 for every post and page, with the average and how many need work.
Search: your clicks and impressions from Google, and the pages and searches that bring them.
Redirects: send old addresses to the right page, and see which missing addresses people ask for.
Local: your business details, printed as structured data for Google and AI assistants.
